methodologyNotes: Covers 8-inch-class (200-216mm blade) Western-profile chef's knives and gyutos a buyer typically cross-shops in 2026, spanning German stamped/forged workhorses, Japanese laminated-steel gyutos, and DTC challenger brands. blade_length_mm is the manufacturer-stated blade length in millimeters (not overall length); where a brand's own spec sheet states a length that differs from its marketing name (e.g. an '8-inch' knife specced at 8.5in), the stated spec is used and the discrepancy is flagged in provenance. steel_type is the alloy/composition as published by the brand (proprietary names like CROMOVA 18 or ACUTO440 are kept verbatim since they are not fungible with generic equivalents). hardness_hrc is the manufacturer- or retailer-published Rockwell hardness; where only a range is published, the midpoint is used and the full range is noted in provenance; null if no figure is published anywhere found. Independent lab-measured hardness (e.g. TechGearLab's own Rockwell testing) frequently reads lower than the manufacturer's spec-sheet figure — both numbers are cited in provenance where available rather than silently choosing one. handle_material is the primary handle material/construction as published. edge_angle_degrees is the factory edge angle per side in degrees as published; where a brand publishes a range or an asymmetric bevel, a representative single figure is used and the exact figure/range is preserved in provenance; null if never published. weight_grams is the knife's own weight (not shipping weight) in grams, preferring a directly-stated gram/ounce figure over a 'shipping weight' figure, which tends to run 30-80g heavier due to packaging; where sources disagree by more than a few grams, the primary source's figure is used and the spread is noted in provenance. full_tang is true only when the brand describes an exposed, handle-length steel tang; knives whose own documentation calls out a 'concealed', 'rat-tail', or 'composite' tang are recorded false even when marketed loosely as 'full tang', with the exact wording preserved in provenance. blade_finish is a short free-text description of the blade's construction/finish (forged vs. stamped, cladding, hand-honing, etc.). priceUsd is a US list/MSRP price for the base configuration (single knife, cheapest handle/color where variants exist); where fetched pages would not statically expose a price (a JS-rendered storefront) and no other retail listing could be confirmed, priceUsd is null rather than guessed, per priceNote. Every product was checked against at least one primary retailer/manufacturer page; most carry a second, independently-fetched corroborating source (an independent test lab, a second retailer, or a specialist importer) — omitted only where a second usable source could not be reached.

products.name: Wüsthof Classic 8-Inch Cook's Knife
products.priceNote: US MSRP $170 for model 1040100120. WebstaurantStore lists $170.00; independently, KnifeCenter, Borsheims, and BBQGuys retail listings found via search all also show $170.00/$169.99, so this is treated as the stable US list price rather than a promo.

specs.blade_finish: Forged, satin-polished, Precision Edge Technology (PEtec) laser-tested edge

products.provenance: wusthof.com itself returned HTTP 429 on every attempt (persistent bot-blocking), so specs were sourced from WebstaurantStore's product page (model 1040100120), which states 8in/1.9in blade height, X50CrMoV15 steel tempered to 58 HRC, POM handle, triple-riveted full tang, and 9.3oz (265g) weight; a second retailer (Heimerdinger Cutlery) independently confirmed 58 HRC via a different phrasing ('tempered to 58 degrees Rockwell') though one aggregated snippet showed a conflicting 56 HRC figure believed to be a transcription error, since 58 HRC is the figure Wusthof's own marketing and the overwhelming majority of retailers use. Weight is recorded as 259g per TechGearLab's own independent measurement (9.1oz) rather than WebstaurantStore's 265g, since TechGearLab directly weighs review units; edge angle of 14 degrees per side (28 inclusive) is Wusthof's published PEtec factory-sharpening angle, corroborated by both TechGearLab and a Wusthof-focused review blog (chefkit.blog). The Wikimedia image is a CC0 'campaign photo' (Kampagnenfoto) of the Classic-line cook's knife uploaded by an account tied to the brand; verified by direct fetch to depict a single Classic-handle chef's knife matching the product's silhouette.

products.name: Victorinox Fibrox Pro 8-Inch Chef's Knife
products.priceNote: Victorinox's own US site (victorinox.com) lists this item (5.2063.20B, sold there as 'Fibrox Chef's Knife Extra Wide') at $67.00 excluding tax. Street price runs well below this: Wasserstrom shows $62.00 and this knife is very commonly discounted to $45-50 at general retailers, but $67 is the figure the brand itself publishes as its price.
products.provenance: Victorinox's own US product page for item 5.2063.20 (the 'wide' 8in Fibrox model commonly sold by other retailers as SKU 47520) directly states a 7.9in/200mm blade, TPE handle, 6.4oz (181g) weight, and $67.00 price, but does not publish an HRC figure or a named steel grade beyond 'high carbon stainless steel'. An independent review (ChefPanko) that weighed and Rockwell-tested a retail unit measured 56 HRC and ~167g, used here to fill the HRC gap the official page leaves open (the 167g vs 181g weight discrepancy is noted; the manufacturer's own stated 181g is kept as the primary spec since it is the brand's own figure for this exact SKU). Multiple retailer listings (Wasserstrom, Amazon) independently describe the construction as a stamped blade with a rat-tail/encapsulated tang rather than an exposed full tang, so full_tang is recorded false despite Victorinox's marketing calling the line 'professional-grade'. The Wikimedia image file is explicitly titled with this SKU (5.2063.20) and was confirmed by direct fetch to show the correct Fibrox-handled chef's knife.

specs.handle_material: Pakkawood, triple-riveted, with stainless steel bolster
specs.blade_finish: Stamped, hollow-ground (Granton/dimpled) edge for reduced food sticking

products.name: Shun Classic 8-Inch Chef's Knife (DM0706)
products.priceNote: Abt.com lists $189.95 for DM0706. Price was observed to vary meaningfully by retailer: Amazon listings around $170 and Shun's own official store around $213 both appear in independent sources, so $189.95 (a mid-market big-box retailer) is used as a representative US price and the spread is disclosed here rather than picking an extreme.

specs.steel_type: VG-MAX stainless steel core, clad in 34 layers per side of Damascus stainless

products.provenance: Abt.com's DM0706 listing states an 8in VG-MAX/Damascus blade, 16-degree per-side edge, D-shaped PakkaWood handle, and a 'full composite tang' (Shun's own term, which the brand and multiple retailers use to mean the tang is a composite/molded construction rather than an exposed steel full tang — recorded here as full_tang: false to reflect the actual construction rather than the marketing phrase), at $189.95. KnivesAcademy independently corroborates 60 HRC and a 7.1oz (201g) weight, which is used in place of WebstaurantStore's 0.67lb (304g) 'shipping weight' figure since it is closer to the knife's actual weight. The product image is a retailer-hosted copy of Shun's own studio photography (confirmed by embedded file metadata naming the exact SKU '921DM0706' and by visual inspection showing the correct Damascus blade and black D-handle with the Shun kanji mark); it is credited to Shun/Kai USA rather than to WebstaurantStore since the photography itself is the brand's.

products.name: Global G-2 8-Inch Chef's Knife
products.priceNote: Global's own US site (globalcutleryusa.com) shows a suggested retail price of $199.93/$199.95 with a current sale price of $149.95; $199.95 (the stated 'suggested retail') is used as the base MSRP figure.

specs.handle_material: Hollow stainless steel, sand-filled for balance, dimpled grip
specs.blade_finish: Convex-ground, satin, one-piece steel monocoque construction

products.provenance: Global's own US product page confirms CROMOVA 18 steel ice-tempered and hardened to '56-58 HRC' (midpoint 57 used) and a sand-filled hollow stainless handle, but does not publish blade length in mm, edge angle, weight, or tang construction in the fetched content. Global's knives are famously a single continuous piece of steel from blade tip through handle (no separate handle/tang junction), so full_tang is recorded true to reflect that the entire knife, not just a tang, is one forged/molded steel piece. NothingButKnives' independent review fills the remaining gaps: 172g measured weight, 7.9in blade, and a convex grind description that 'starts around 12 degrees' (used as the edge_angle figure since Global does not publish a fixed bevel angle for its convex edge). The product image is fetched directly from Global's own site and was confirmed by visible blade etching reading 'GLOBAL CROMOVA 18 Stainless Steel G-2 YOSHIKIN Japan'.

products.name: Misen 8-Inch Chef's Knife (ACUTO440)
products.priceNote: Misen's own current storefront (misen.pro) prices the 8in Chef's Knife (ACUTO440 steel) at $124.00. TechGearLab separately tested an earlier/different 8in Misen unit (AUS-10 steel) at a $94 list price; both figures are disclosed since they may reflect different product generations.

specs.steel_type: AICHI ACUTO440 stainless steel (current line, per misen.pro); the unit independently tested by TechGearLab was AUS-10 stainless, suggesting a steel change across Misen's product versions

products.provenance: Misen's current storefront (misen.pro) states ACUTO440 stainless steel, 0.5lb (227g) weight, and a $124 price for the 8in Chef's Knife, but does not publish HRC, edge angle, or handle material composition in the fetched content. TechGearLab's independent, hands-on review of an 8in Misen chef's knife fills those gaps (measured 53 HRC, 14.25-degree measured edge angle, 'Polymer' handle, 238g measured weight, $94 list) but describes the steel as AUS-10 rather than ACUTO440 and cites a lower price, which likely reflects an earlier product generation/SKU rather than a data error; both are disclosed rather than silently merged. Marketing copy from multiple retailers independently and consistently describes this knife as full-tang. The product image is fetched directly from Misen's own CDN and was confirmed by visible 'MISEN' blade etching and the brand's signature blue handle.

products.name: Made In 8-Inch Chef Knife
products.priceNote: madeincookware.com renders its price client-side (JavaScript), so no static price could be extracted from the fetched page after repeated attempts, including scanning for JSON-LD/meta price tags. Third-party listings (Walmart, Amazon) that would carry the price could also not be retrieved (bot-verification walls). Third-party reviews describe this knife as sitting in a roughly $99-$139 band depending on handle material, but that figure was not independently confirmed against a live price and is not used as priceUsd per the 'null beats a guess' rule.

specs.handle_material: Synthetic resin (POM-like) or wood (olive wood/amaranth wood/walnut), triple/double-riveted

products.provenance: Made In's own product page (fetched directly) states a blade length of 8.5in (~216mm, despite the product being named the '8-Inch Chef Knife' — the naming/spec discrepancy is real and preserved rather than silently corrected), X50CrMoV15 nitrogen-treated steel at '58+ HRC', an 18-degree stated edge angle with an asymmetric 14/4-degree double bevel, full-tang fully-forged construction, and 7oz (198g) weight. Prudent Reviews' independent review broadly corroborates the steel and full-tang claims but reports a different edge-angle framing (12.5 degrees per side / 25 degrees total) and a heavier measured weight (0.5lb/227g); both the official spec and the independent figures are disclosed given the conflict rather than picking one silently. Price could not be confirmed: the manufacturer's own page does not statically expose it and Walmart/Amazon listings found via search returned bot-verification challenge pages on every fetch attempt, so priceUsd is null. No confirmed-matching image could be retrieved for the same reason (the storefront's image URLs are also injected client-side), so the image field is omitted.

products.name: Tojiro DP F-808 Gyuto (210mm)
products.priceNote: ChefKnivesToGo lists $139.00 (sold there under the name 'Tojiro Classic,' which the listing itself states is 'formerly known as Tojiro DP', i.e. the same F-808 product under updated branding). Other importers price the same knife lower: Japan Knife Shop $119.00, and TechGearLab's tested unit carried a $128 list price.

specs.steel_type: VG-10 stainless steel core, 3-layer (San Mai) clad with 13-chrome stainless

products.provenance: ChefKnivesToGo's listing for the F-808 (explicitly cross-referenced as the classic Tojiro DP) states VG-10 San Mai construction at HRC 60, a black Micarta Western handle with stainless bolster and triple rivets, full tang, 212mm blade (210mm nominal used), and 7.2oz (204g) weight, at $139. A second Tojiro DP importer (Japan Knife Shop) independently corroborates the VG-10/'cobalt alloy steel' composition and 210mm blade length but reports a lighter 180g weight and a lower $119 price; TechGearLab's independent lab test of the same DP Gyuto line measured 193g and a lower 51 HRC against the specced 60 HRC (a common spec-vs-measured gap seen throughout this dataset) at $128 list. All three weight and price figures are disclosed since they do not fully agree; the ChefKnivesToGo figures are used as primary since that source gave the most complete, internally consistent spec set. No source published a specific edge-angle-in-degrees figure (TechGearLab's 12.5-degree figure is a measured, not stated, angle, so it is not used as the spec value), so edge_angle_degrees is null. The product image, hosted on ChefKnivesToGo's own CDN, was confirmed by direct fetch to show a black Western-handled gyuto with visible Japanese maker stamping.
